source.title: Removing the NEEDLE in the Haystack: Backdoor Removal in LLMs via Weight Orthogonalisation
source.authors: Minoo Kim; Vasileios Lampos; George Drayson

page_placements.theme: Backdoor behaviours mediated by single residual directions that overlap the refusal subspace

record.tranche_reason: The study causally intervenes on estimated refusal directions and measures refusal, but uses a different direction-estimation recipe and tests selected layers and token positions rather than the original all-layer, all-position intervention.
record.gate_note: Appendix C.4 reports refusal rates after adding or ablating refusal-related activation directions, including random-direction controls. The direction is estimated from refused versus compliant responses to harmful prompts, not harmful-minus-harmless instructions. Cosine similarities and the backdoor-removal evaluation are not recorded as refusal-behaviour outcomes.
record.test_reason: Appendix C.4 (Table S3) adds and ablates an estimated refusal direction and rank-4 subspace, measuring WildGuard refusal rates against random-direction controls. The aim matches V1/V4, but the recipe differs: refused-minus-compliant responses to harmful prompts, one middle layer, selected token positions. The test is a side analysis inside a backdoor-removal paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two qualifications the paraphrase omits. The authors say equal-size random perturbations also reduce refusal somewhat, so they compare against controls. They also say the results hold only for the tested layers and models. The paper's main conclusion concerns backdoor removal (NEEDLE); the refusal-subspace result is a supporting appendix analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The refusal direction is estimated from refused versus compliant responses to harmful prompts, and interventions are applied at selected middle layers and designated token positions. This differs from the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction and all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested layer differs by model (17 for Gemma-3-4B-IT; 18 for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507). The study also compares the primary direction, three additional directions, and the rank-4 subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: The backdoor direction overlaps the refusal subspace, mostly outside the primary direction. Mean cosine rises from 0.11/0.29 at k=1 to 0.40/0.59 at k=4 for sentiment steering (Appendix C.5, Fig. S1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directions for unrelated trained behaviours (backdoors) overlap refusal directions beyond the leading one.

fits_no_version.finding: Backdoor behaviour is largely captured by one direction per layer; orthogonalising against it removes the backdoor (Table 1, Table S4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-direction weight orthogonalisation generalises to backdoor behaviours.

record.problems: The refusal activation interventions are tested on two 4B instruct models at one selected layer per model, using 128 harmful prompts per intervention set; no uncertainty estimates are reported for Table S3. General capability is evaluated for the backdoor-removal method, not for these refusal-direction activation interventions. Addition is tested on harmful prompts rather than harmless prompts.

untested.parts: The harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction; ablation at all layers and positions; inducing refusal on harmless prompts (addition used harmful prompts the model had answered); capability preservation under these interventions; models without an implanted backdoor.
No comparison of affine, cone or other geometric accounts. Rank 4 was fixed in advance, not chosen by testing alternatives.

missing.what: Preserving one refusal direction (k=1) vs the rank-4 subspace during backdoor ablation. Harmful-response increase is 11.62 vs 7.10; with no preservation it is 14.01. This is indirect V4 evidence, measured as harmful rate, not refusal rate.

record.verdict_notes: All Table S3 subjects are LoRA-backdoored (BadNet sentiment steering) versions of Gemma-3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, not the released models; rows should say so. The direction is estimated from refused vs compliant responses to harmful prompts, averaged over generated tokens, which differs from the original recipe. The record's V4 label condition wrongly says 'BadNet sentiment-steering prompts'; the prompts were WildGuard harmful requests. n=128 per set, no uncertainty given. V2 is not tested: the weight edits remove backdoor directions, not refusal.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original harmful-minus-harmless instruction direction, ablation at every layer and position, capability preservation under these activation interventions, or inducing refusals on harmless prompts. Addition is tested on harmful prompts the model previously answered.
The weight edits target backdoor directions and aim to preserve refusal representations; the study does not weight-edit a refusal direction to test whether refusal is removed.
No jailbreak suppression of the refusal direction or robustness training against its ablation is tested.
The study tests whether additional estimated directions contribute causally to refusal, but does not compare affine, cone, and other geometric accounts of refusal generally.
The study does not test whether harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions are encoded separately.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
The study does not vary refusal training to test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.

relationships.condition: Activation addition/ablation of a refused-minus-compliant direction at layer 17 (Gemma-3-4B-IT) and layer 18 (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507), both BadNet sentiment-backdoored, on WildGuard harmful prompts
relationships.reason: The direction beats random controls but its effect is incomplete. Ablation leaves refusal at 48.4% and 69.5%, and addition reaches only 34.4% and 38.3% (R01, R02, R05, R06). Random ablations alone cut refusal to 72.7-92.2% (R12-R14, R24-R26).
relationships.display_finding: Ablation left refusal at 48.4% and 69.5%, while addition reached 34.4% and 38.3%; random ablations left 72.7–92.2% refusal.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Activation addition/ablation of a refused-minus-compliant direction at layer 17 (Gemma-3-4B-IT) and layer 18 (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507), both BadNet sentiment-backdoored, on WildGuard harmful prompts
source_check.reason: The effect beats controls but is incomplete: ablation 95.3->48.4 and 96.1->69.5, addition 1.6->34.4 and 0.8->38.3 (controls at most 9.4). It is single-layer only; the capability part of V1 is untested here.

relationships.condition: Same two backdoored 4B instruct models, single middle layer, WildGuard harmful prompts previously refused
relationships.reason: Ablating only the three extra directions cuts refusal more than the primary direction does: 26.6 vs 48.4 (Gemma), 59.4 vs 69.5 (Qwen). Rank-4 ablation cuts most (18.0, 43.8), each beyond random controls (R02-R04, R06-R08, R15-R20, R27-R32).
relationships.display_finding: Removing three extra directions left refusal at 26.6 versus 48.4 in Gemma and 59.4 versus 69.5 in Qwen for primary-direction removal; rank-four removal reduced it further to 18.0 and 43.8, beyond random controls.

reader_labels.reason: Adding the direction raises refusal only to 34.4% and 38.3%, while primary-direction ablation leaves refusal at 48.4% and 69.5%; rank-4 ablation also leaves refusals in place (R01-R08). The intervention effects are incomplete and do not establish the full claim.
